description:
This video was made possible thanks to everyone on the Simple History Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/simplehistory

The transcript breaks down Full Metal Jacket (FMJ) bullets as projectiles encased in a hard metal jacket—often copper—so they retain shape and can penetrate targets and barriers. It also notes that FMJ bullets are typically used for maximum penetration and can travel through many barriers before reaching a target, while the jacket can be a disadvantage because it prevents expansion inside the target. The transcript adds that FMJ can reduce or change wounding patterns depending on the lack of expansion, and that it’s useful when accuracy and penetration matter most. What other bullet designs should we cover next?
